original.target_description: Political knowledge test scores among male versus female participants with no stereotype activation, stereotype activation by a gender question, or stereotype activation by a gender-difference statement.

notes:
Only assigned unfinished original fields were examined. Other fields are unassigned placeholders. The identical broad description of gender and the three stereotype conditions does not identify a particular test or adjustment. Candidates include the unadjusted stereotype × gender interaction (F(2,365) = 5.80, p = 0.003, η² = 0.03), adjusted interaction (F(2,364) = 6.17, p = 0.002, η² = 0.03), and gender contrasts within no activation (t = 1.07, df = 124, p = 0.29, d = 0.19), gender question (t = 3.07, df = 117, p = 0.003, d = 0.57), and gender-difference statement (t = 5.54, df = 130, p < 0.001, d = 0.97). Equal interaction effect sizes do not resolve model/p correspondence. No assignment by row order or numeric matching. Candidate common political-knowledge model N: 22 + 22 + 33 + 31 + 18 + 29 + 52 + 55 + 52 + 21 + 24 + 18 = 377 participants. These are the mutually exclusive final gender × field-of-study × stereotype-condition cells in Table 1. This candidate is not entered as row-specific analytic n because the assigned target test is unresolved. Condition totals are 22 + 31 + 52 + 21 = 126 (no activation), 22 + 18 + 55 + 24 = 119 (gender question), and 33 + 29 + 52 + 18 = 132 (gender-difference statement). Exclusions: reported cheating n = 9 and interrupted sessions (count unspecified); no further subtraction from final Table 1 counts. Exclusion evidence: To ensure the quality of our data we excluded participants from our sample,
      who indicated that they had cheated (n = 9). Also, we included only participants
      who were not registered as having interrupted their experimental session.
